newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU Court upholds strict UK border controls.
newsitem.headline: EU Court upholds strict UK border controls.

text.p: Britain already has the right to stop European Union nationals from entering the country, the EU's highest court ruled on Tuesday.
Britain's new Prime Minister Tony Blair is fighting and apparently winning a battle at the EU summit in Amsterdam to keep border controls at a time when his continental partners are abolishing them.
The rest of the EU is scrapping internal border checks in favour of once-only checks at the EU's external borders. But Britain argues that as an island all its borders are external.

Responding to a query from Britain's High Court of Justice, the European Court of Justice stated that existing EU law allows Britain to keep out other EU nationals if it can demonstrate a need to protect public safety.

The British court was seeking guidance in separate cases brought by Mann Singh Shingara, a French national, and Abbas Radiom, who has both Irish and Iranian nationality, against the refusal to allow them to stay in Britain.
The EU treaty and adopted legislation allow member states to refuse entry to Community nationals on grounds of public policy, security or health.

The court ruling upheld Britain's policy of keeping out people suspected of being security risks, but said it could not refuse entry to an EU national without an independent judicial review, nor could it keep a ban in place forever if a subsequent review is requested.
The court said an EU national banned from entering another member state was entitled to a review of the ban if the reassons for imposing it no longer existed.
